Apple has removed a billboard in Milan depicting a child holding an iPhone, which was part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign. Details as follows.

Apple removes controversial Italian billboard

A few days ago, Italy's child welfare watchdog, the Authority for Children and Adolescents (Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza, AGIA), condemned Apple over the depiction of children holding iPhones in its "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign.

The campaign focuses on the durability and ruggedness of the iPhone, showing iPhones being dirtied, dropped, or used in ways that might damage them — including someone taking photos in heavy rain, someone watching videos at the edge of a bathtub, a dog chewing on an iPhone, and a child clumsily holding the phone.

After a billboard depicting the last scene was erected on via Melchiorre Gioia in Milan, AGIA received a letter from a member of the public saying the ad normalised the phenomenon of the "electronic babysitter".

AGIA agreed with this view and referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian Competition Authority AGCM, and the country's advertising self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate examination and any action".

Now, according to Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has removed the controversial billboard and replaced it with one promoting the device's "Find My" feature.

Apple has yet to publicly respond to the incident, but the company's swift action reflects how seriously it takes the criticism, even though an ad intended to showcase iPhone durability has been interpreted in a completely different way by the public.

What do you think of the controversy? Let us know in the comments.
